夢を見ている。
　曖昧な、とくに意味などない、灼けたアメのようなユメを見ている。
　彼女のことが、好きなのか。
　感情の正体はわからないけど、どうしても気になってしまうのは、もう否定しようのない事実だと思う。

Do I love her?
I don’t know what this feeling is. But there is no longer any denying that I can’t stop thinking about her.

彼女のことが、好きなのか。
　……わからない。
ただ、自分がどうにかしてしまいそうな時、助けてくれたのは彼女だけだ。

　雨にうたれて、あのまま本当に死んでいたかもしれない。

lines.maoEnglish:
Do I love her?
…I don’t know. I know only that when I was about to lose myself, she alone saved me.
Without her.
I might truly have died there in the rain.

I may have just died under the pouring rain.

lines.japanese:
「―――志貴さま」
　……朝の光に交じって、翡翠の呼び声が聞こえてくる。
「―――志貴さま、お時間です。
お目覚めください」
　抑揚のない翡翠の声に、意識がはっきりと覚めていく。
lines.label: s260
lines.maoEnglish:
“—Master Shiki.”
Hisui’s voice reached me through the morning light.
“Master Shiki, it is time. Please wake up.”
Her level, uninflected voice drew me fully into consciousness.
lines.mao_english:

"---Shiki-sama, it is time.
Please wake up."

「――――――」
　目を覚ましたとたん、厭なモノが視界に入ってきた。
　ずきり、とこめかみには銃創のような頭痛。
「あ――――」
　起きたばかりの意識が、がらり、と足場を失っていく。
　そのまま眩暈を起こしてしまう前に、急いで枕元のメガネを手に取った。
lines.label: s260
lines.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
The instant I opened my eyes, something hateful filled my vision.
Pain shot through my temple like a bullet wound.
“Ah—”
My newly awakened mind lost the ground beneath it.
Before vertigo could take me, I snatched the glasses from my bedside.

「……いや、そういうわけじゃなんだ。

「そんなことより、おはよう翡翠。
起こしにきてくれてありがとう」

lines.label: s260
lines.maoEnglish:
“Master Shiki…? Are you feeling unwell?”
“…No, it’s nothing like that. Just a little anemia.”
I shook my head, banishing what I had seen from memory.
“Never mind that. Good morning, Hisui. Thanks for waking me.”
Sitting up, I gave her the most natural smile I could manage.

lines.japanese:
「いえ、これがわたしの仕事ですから。
志貴さまに感謝されるほどのことではありません」
「そうかな、俺はすごくありがたいけど。
目覚し時計の音なんかより、何倍もあったかい感じがする」
　ベッドから立ちあがる。
　時刻は朝の七時前―――いつもより十分ほど早い時間。
「……ああ、朝ごはんだろ？
　すぐに行くから先に行っててくれ」
lines.label: s260
lines.maoEnglish:
“It is only my duty. There is no need for Master Shiki to thank me.”
“Maybe, but I’m really grateful. Waking to your voice feels so much warmer than an alarm clock.”
I rose from bed.
It was not yet seven—about ten minutes earlier than usual.
“…Breakfast, right? I’ll be down in a minute. Go on ahead.”

"…… Hmm, breakfast?
I'll be there soon, so please go ahead of me."

lines.japanese:
「それなのですが、志貴さま。
その―――秋葉さまが、志貴さまに問い詰めたい事がある、と居間でお待ちになっておられます」
　言いにくそうに翡翠はそんなコトを言ってくる。
「……問い詰めたいコトって……あいつ、もしかしてご機嫌ななめ……？」
「……はい。
志貴さまが昨夜遅くに出かけた事を、お気づきになられたようです」
「……あ」
　思わず声をあげてしまった。
　昨夜はつい勢いにまかせてアルクェイドを捜しに行って、夜遅くに帰ってきてしまったんだっけ。
lines.label: s260
lines.maoEnglish:
“About that, Master Shiki—Miss Akiha is waiting in the sitting room. She says she has something she wishes to question Master Shiki about.”
Hisui looked distinctly uncomfortable.
“You mean she wants to question me because she’s angry?”
“Yes. She appears to have discovered that Master Shiki went out late last night.”
“Oh.”
The sound escaped before I could stop it.
Last night I had rushed off to find Arcueid on impulse and come home in the small hours.

Sudden attacks of vertigo. Headaches. Anemia.
I couldn’t count how many things they had forced me to surrender.

That human life is not precious, but must be treasured because it can never be restored?

If a thing disappeared that readily, hadn’t it been worth that little from the start?
Calling it precious was meaningless.

“I have to get to school.”
I had to go and see Ciel.
Enduring the ache that lingered like a knot in the corner of my skull, I left my room.

lines.maoEnglish:
“You see, vampiric species recover from most wounds.
Ordinary external forces—weapons, in plain language—cannot damage them faster than they can restore themselves.
To destroy one, you need either an external force powerful enough to outpace that restoration or one that nullifies the restoration itself.
“Their curse of restoration is not true healing, but a reversal of time that returns a damaged part to its former state. Mysteries capable of negating that curse are known as conceptual weapons.”

“Their curse of restoration is not true healing, but a reversal of time that returns a damaged part to its former state. Mysteries capable of negating that curse are known as conceptual weapons.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Let's see, vampires have the ability to recover from most injuries they receive.
With ordinary outside force…… I mean normal weapons.
With such things, you cannot cause wounds greater than the speed of their recovery.
To kill a vampire, you need an outside force greater than their speed of recovery, or something that nullifies their ability to recover.
This ability of theirs, the curse of restoration---actually isn't treating the wounds.
Instead, it is a reversing of time to restore the damaged body part back to its original state.
An occult artifact which nullifies this effect is called a conceptual weapon."

Even a vampire ceases to exist if both body and soul are destroyed. Kill a vampire, and it dies. The ‘Serpent,’ however, found a way around that.”

Even if they are vampires, if you destroy their body and soul, they will be vanquished.
If you kill a vampire, they will die.
But 'The Serpent' is a vampire who has conquered even this."

lines.japanese:
「遠野くんは輪廻転生という言葉をご存知ですか？
　仏教用語ですから日本の方には馴染みはあると思うんですけど」
「……ああ、あるよ。
死んでも次の人間として生まれ変わるっていうヤツだろ」
「はい、その通りです」
「ようするにですね。
　『蛇』と呼ばれる吸血鬼は、その輪廻転生を自分の物にしてしまっているんです。
　殺しても生き返る、というのはそういう意味です」
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
“Are you familiar with reincarnation, Tohno? It is a Buddhist concept, so I imagine most Japanese people know it.”
“Sure. You die and are reborn as someone else.”
“Exactly.”
“The point is simple.
The vampire called the ‘Serpent’ has made reincarnation his own.
That is what I mean when I say he returns to life after being killed.”
lines.mao_english:

“Exactly.”

The vampire called the ‘Serpent’ has made reincarnation his own.
That is what I mean when I say he returns to life after being killed.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Tohno-kun, are you familiar with the cycle of reincarnation?
It is part of Buddhist doctrine, so I would think a Japanese would be quite familiar with it."
"…… Yeah.
It's that thing where when someone dies, they are reborn again as another human."
"Yes, exactly."
"In other words,
The vampire named 'The Serpent' has made this cycle of reincarnation his own.
That's what I mean when I say he comes back to life even after he is killed."

lines.japanese:
「輪廻転生って―――ようするに、死んだらまた赤ん坊からやり直すっていう、こと……？」
「そうです。
『蛇』は存命している間に、次の自分の肉体をあらかじめ決めておいて、その赤子が誕生した時点で『自分』の全情報を移植します。
　『蛇』の情報はその赤子が成人、ないし自己としての知性を持つまで影を潜めています。
　『自分』を引き継ぐに相応しい知性をもった段階で、その赤子は『蛇』という吸血鬼になってしまうんです」
「―――ちょっと待って先輩。
それってなに、まさか赤ん坊が母親の中にいる時に手術とかをするっていうことなのか……？」
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
“Reincarnation… So when he dies, he starts over as a baby?”
“Yes. While still alive, the ‘Serpent’ selects the body that will become his next incarnation, and at the child’s birth, he implants the entirety of himself within it.
That information remains dormant until the child reaches adulthood, or at least develops a mature sense of self.
Once its mind becomes capable of inheriting him, the child becomes the Serpent himself.”
“Wait, Ciel. Are you saying he performs some kind of operation while the baby is still in its mother?”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Reincarnation---you mean if he dies he will start over again as a baby……?"
"Yes.
While 'The Serpent' is alive, he chooses his next host and when it is born, he transmits all of the information of his 'self'.
'The Serpent's' information stays deep within the baby until it matures, or until it gains sufficient intelligence.
As soon as that baby has the intelligence to succeed 'his self', the baby becomes a new vampire that is the 'Serpent'."
"---Wait a minute.
What's that?
Don't tell me that he does surgery on it while it's in the mother or something like that."

lines.japanese:
「いいえ、医学的な手段ではないんです。
　だって『蛇』は今の自分の肉体が滅ぼされた瞬間に、あらかじめ『次はこの母体にしよう』と決めておいたモノに転生するんですから。
　さきほどは『全情報』といいましたけど、解りやすく言えば『魂』ですね。
　魂が大気を伝搬して他者に乗り移る、なんていうのは実感が湧かないでしょうけど、ようするに電波と同じなんです。
　この場合、電波を発信するのも受信するのも人間の脳。
　カレの優れたところは、魂なんていう計測不能にして、肉体という器から離れたら霧散してしまうモノを、伝達可能なモノとして加工したことでしょう」
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
“No. There is nothing medical about it.
The instant his current body is destroyed, the ‘Serpent’ reincarnates through the womb he selected in advance.
I called it his ‘complete information,’ but in simpler terms, it is his soul.
A soul passing through the air to possess another person may be difficult to imagine, but it functions much like a radio signal.
In this case, human brains serve as both transmitter and receiver.
His great achievement was turning the soul—something immeasurable that normally disperses when separated from the vessel of the body—into something that could be transmitted.”
lines.mao_english:
“No. There is nothing medical about it.
The instant his current body is destroyed, the ‘Serpent’ reincarnates through the womb he selected in advance.
I called it his ‘complete information,’ but in simpler terms, it is his soul.
A soul passing through the air to possess another person may be difficult to imagine, but it functions much like a radio signal.
In this case, human brains serve as both transmitter and receiver.
His great achievement was turning the soul—something immeasurable that normally disperses when separated from the vessel of the body—into something that could be transmitted.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"No, it's not anything medical.
Because the instant his body is destroyed, he reincarnates into the body he chose as his next host.

"I said all of his information earlier, but to say it simpler, think of it as his 'soul'.
It wouldn't be quite correct to say his soul propagates through the air and takes over someone's body, but it's similar to an electro-magnetic wave.
In this case, the human brain is what does the transmitting and the receiving.
His exceptional point is that he took this soul, which is incalculable and something that disperses as soon as it leaves the envelope of the body, and processed it as something that could be transmitted."

We enjoy nature’s gifts even as we plunder it, and even if nature perishes, we intend to survive.
Perhaps the only reason we became the dominant species on Earth is that humanity alone acquired that particular sin.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"We humans have flourished this much by isolating ourselves from nature.
While we receive blessings from nature, we steal from it, and even if nature is destroyed, we will not be destroyed.
We became the most superior race on this planet probably because of this one sin only we humans carry."

lines.japanese:
「わたしたちは自然とはもう融け合えない。
そのかわりに自然、つまりこの星さえ破壊しえる業を手に入れました。
　けれど、自然にしてみればそれは悪です。
世界だって一つの生命なんですから、自身をわたしたちから守ろうという意思が働きます。
　けれど世界には触覚がない。
　だから―――わたしたちをいさめる分身を、わたしたちと同じように自然と乖離したカタチとして生み出します」
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
“We can no longer merge with nature. In exchange, we gained the means to destroy nature—even the planet itself.
To nature, that makes us evil. The world is a living thing as well, and so it possesses the will to defend itself against us.
But the world has no senses of its own.
It therefore creates avatars to restrain humanity, giving them independent forms severed from nature just as we are.”
lines.mao_english:
“We can no longer merge with nature. In exchange, we gained the means to destroy nature—even the planet itself.
To nature, that makes us evil. The world is a living thing as well, and so it possesses the will to defend itself against us.
But the world has no senses of its own.
It therefore creates avatars to restrain humanity, giving them independent forms severed from nature just as we are.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"We can no longer be a part of nature.
In its place, we have gained ways to even destroy nature, this whole planet.
However, from the nature's perspective, this is evil.
The world itself is a form of life, so it has the will to protect itself from us.
But it does not have senses.
So---it creates a presence, separated from nature like us, to remonstrate us."

lines.japanese:
……先輩はおかしい。
　自然に意思なんかあるわけない。
　そう、あるわけがない―――だが、それは単に感じ取れないだけではないのか。
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
…She was talking nonsense.
Nature could not possess a will.
Of course it couldn’t—and yet, perhaps the truth was simply that I could not perceive it.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
…… Senpai is weird.
Nature doesn't have a will of its own.
Yeah, it can't---but, can it be that we just can't feel it?
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
自然に、世界に意思はある。
だからこそ今も存在していて、美しく保とうとする。
　問題は、それが感じとれないというコトではなく。
　自然が美しいと思う基準と、人間が美しいと思う基準が同じだということだ。
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
Nature—the world—possessed a will. That was why it still endured, why it strove to preserve its beauty.
The question was not whether humanity could sense it.
The question was why nature’s idea of beauty should resemble our own.
lines.mao_english:

The question was why nature’s idea of beauty should resemble our own.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Nature, the earth, possesses a will.
That is why it still exists and tries to stay beautiful.
The problem isn't that we can't feel it.
It's that the standard of what nature thinks is beautiful and the standard of what humans believe is beautiful are the same.

lines.japanese:
「自然、世界が自らの触覚として独立させた存在。
それが一般に神霊、精霊と呼ばれるモノたちです。
　動物霊が現世に残り続けて『霊体』として残ったモノとはそもそも存在の次元が違う超越種たち。
　真祖というのはその一種族なんです。
　もとから人間をいさめる役割として生まれた彼らは、人間を悪としか思っていない。
　わたしたちが人間を捕食する吸血鬼を『悪』と思うように、彼らにとって自然を食い物にする人間は『悪』なんです」
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
“The independent beings nature created as its senses are commonly called Divine Spirits and Elementals. They are transcendent beings on an entirely different plane from animal ghosts that linger in this world as spiritual bodies.
True Ancestors are one such species.
Born to restrain humanity, they see us only as evil.
Just as we call vampires evil for preying upon humans, they call humans evil for feeding upon nature.”
lines.mao_english:
“The independent beings nature created as its senses are commonly called Divine Spirits and Elementals. They are transcendent beings on an entirely different plane from animal ghosts that linger in this world as spiritual bodies.
True Ancestors are one such species.
Born to restrain humanity, they see us only as evil.
Just as we call vampires evil for preying upon humans, they call humans evil for feeding upon nature.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"An existence which the world created to sense for it.
These are what we usually call spirits.
They are a transcendental species existing on another plane different from the remaining spirits of animals in the present world.
The True Ancestors are one type of these spirits.
They are born with the purpose to punish humans, so they only see humans as evil.
Much as we think vampires who prey upon humans are evil, they view humans who prey upon nature as evil."

lines.japanese:
「―――真祖にとって人間は敵にすぎません。
　もともと自然の一部、いえこの世界そのものとリンクしている彼らの能力は、それこそ際限というものがないんです。
　……教会の長い歴史の中でも、真祖と戦った記録は数えるほどしかありません。
　彼らは世界そのものから力を引き上げる。
　だから、彼らを倒すということは世界を倒すほどの概念武装が必要になります。
　……もちろん、そんな武装はありません。
　ですから彼らには、外的要因による『死』を与えることができない」
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
“To True Ancestors, humans are merely enemies.
Their power is linked to nature—to the world itself—and therefore knows no limit.
In all the Church’s long history, there are only a handful of recorded battles against them.
They draw their strength directly from the world.
To defeat one would require a conceptual weapon capable of defeating the world itself.
No such weapon exists.
Thus no outside force can impose ‘death’ upon them.”
lines.mao_english:

No such weapon exists.
Thus no outside force can impose ‘death’ upon them.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"---Humans are only enemies to the True Ancestors.

…… Of course, such a weapon does not exist.
So that means their 'death' cannot be caused by external factors."

あの夜。
　ホテルの一室で彼女は言った。
　遠野志貴が彼女を殺そうとしたときが夜であったのなら、たとえこの目でも彼女から死を視るコトはできなかった、と。
　つまり。
　それは、死なないというコトだ。

In the hotel room, she had told me.

In other words.
She would not die.

lines.japanese:
「いいですか、遠野くん。
　アルクェイド・ブリュンスタッドが『蛇』を追っているのは、『蛇』に与えてしまった自分の力を取り戻すためなんです。
　それは決して人間のためなんかじゃない。
　どうして今の彼女があんなに弱っているかは知りませんけど、もし力が戻れば―――遠野くんに手を貸してもらう必要なんてなくなる。
　その時、彼女が遠野くんを無事に帰すと思いますか？」
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
“Listen carefully, Tohno.
Arcueid Brunestud pursues the ‘Serpent’ so she can reclaim the power she gave him.
She is not doing this for humanity.
I don’t know why she is presently so weak, but once her power returns, she will no longer need your help.
When that happens, do you truly believe she will let you walk away unharmed?”
lines.mao_english:
“Listen carefully, Tohno.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Do you understand, Tohno-kun?
Arcueid Brunestud is pursuing 'The Serpent' in order to recover her power he took away from her.
It's not for the sake of any humans.
I don't know why she is weakened now, but if she regains her power---she will not need your help, Tohno-kun.
When that happens, do you think she will let you leave safely?"

「……………帰すに決まってる、だろ。
　だって―――あいつが俺をどうにかするなんて、そんな理由ないんだから」

lines.maoEnglish:

She has no reason to do anything to me.”

lines.japanese:
「彼女は吸血鬼です。
それも死徒たちのように、自分が生き延びるために他人の血を必要とする吸血種じゃない。
　いいですか遠野くん。
真祖たちが人間から血を吸わなければ、そもそも吸血鬼なんていう存在は生まれなかった。
　彼らは―――人間の血なんか吸わなくても生きていけるくせに、ただ吸いたいっていう衝動だけで人間の血を吸って、人間を人間外のものにしてしまうんです。
　そんなモノの傍に、一般人である貴方を歩かせるわけにはいきません」
lines.label: s267
lines.maoEnglish:
“She is a vampire—but unlike the Dead Apostles, she does not need human blood to survive.
Understand this, Tohno: if the True Ancestors had never drunk human blood, vampires would never have existed.
They can live perfectly well without it, yet they drink from human beings solely because the impulse takes them, transforming their victims into things no longer human.
I cannot allow an ordinary person like you to walk beside such a creature.”
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"She is a vampire.
She isn't like the Dead Apostles who suck blood in order to prolong their own life.
Look, Tohno-kun.
If the True Ancestors didn't suck human blood, vampires would never exist in the first place.
They---can survive without sucking human blood, but they still do suck blood because they have the urge to do so, and make humans into an existence outside of human nature.
I can't let some ordinary person like you be with her."

Maybe it was because my head had been swimming, but everything she’d said seemed to concern somebody else.

「それじゃあ彼女にはもう協力しないでくださいね」
「それは―――」
　それは、できない。
　先輩の言っている事は納得できない。
　だって。
先輩はアルクェイドを知らない。
　あいつがいいヤツなんだって、知らないクセに。

lines.maoEnglish:
“Tohno. Do you understand now just how dangerous she is?”
“Yeah. I mean, I understand the words, more or less.”
“Then please don’t help her anymore.”
“That’s—”
I couldn’t do that.
What Ciel was saying didn’t sit right with me.
Because. Ciel didn’t know Arcueid.
She didn’t know what a good person Arcueid really was.

It took hard soles—lace-up boots, perhaps—to produce a rhythm so crisp.
…Not that I needed to speculate.
The footsteps pattering after me had unquestionably come from lace-up boots.

“Both of you, wait. I told you to calm down…!”
Bracing myself against the pressure in the air, I drew breath from deep in my belly and shouted.
“…”
“…”
For one instant, both of them stopped breathing.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… Wait you two, please.
I said to calm down……!"
Ignoring the tension in the air, I yell out.
"----"
"----"
For an instant, they both stop.
lines.mirror_moon:

"----"
"----"

lines.japanese:
その後に、ダン、と地面を蹴る音が二つ。
―――俺の怒声が最後の引き金になったのか。
　白い影と黒い影は、寄せ合う磁極のように衝突した。
lines.label: s270
lines.maoEnglish:
Then came two simultaneous cracks as their feet struck the ground.
―――Perhaps my shout had pulled the final trigger.
The white shadow and the black collided like opposite magnetic poles snapping together.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
After that, the sound of two feet kicking the earth.
---My shout must have triggered the start.
The white and black figures crash into each other as if they were two magnets of opposite polarity.

lines.japanese:
二人の戦いは、正直俺の理解の及ぶところではなかった。
　アルクェイドの体の動きは、とてもじゃないけど目で追っていけない。
　ただ、夜の闇に白い残像が流れていっているようにしか見えない。
　驚くべきなのは、そんなアルクェイドを前にして一歩も引かない先輩の姿だった。
lines.label: s270
lines.maoEnglish:
Their battle lay frankly beyond my comprehension.
Arcueid moved far too quickly for my eyes to follow.
All I saw was a stream of white afterimages through the night.
What astonished me was that Ciel refused to yield a single step before her.
lines.mao_english:

What astonished me was that Ciel refused to yield a single step before her.
lines.mirrorMoon:
The fight between the two of them is beyond me.
Arcueid's body movement isn't something I can track with my eyes.
All I can see is a white blur running through the night.
What's surprising is that Senpai does not even back off seeing Arcueid's speed.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
先輩は別段、アルクェイドのように常識外れのスピードとか動きをするわけじゃない。
　ちゃんと地面に足をつけて、的確に矢のようなアルクェイドの猛攻をさばいている。
　第三者的に見て、二人の戦闘能力は伯仲している。
　けれど、先輩自身が口にしていたとおり、アルクェイドの能力というものに限界はないみたいだ。
lines.label: s270
lines.maoEnglish:
Ciel did not move with anything like Arcueid’s impossible speed.
Her feet remained firmly on the ground as she met and deflected every stroke of that arrow-fast assault.
From where I stood, they seemed evenly matched.
But as Ciel herself had said, there appeared to be no ceiling to Arcueid’s power.
lines.mao_english:

From where I stood, they seemed evenly matched.
But as Ciel herself had said, there appeared to be no ceiling to Arcueid’s power.
lines.mirrorMoon:
It's not like Senpai moves with Arcueid's amazing speed.
But she accurately deflects Arcueid's blazing attacks while standing on the ground.
As a third person looking on, their strengths are equal.
However, just like Senpai said, Arcueid's power seems limitless.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
いくら先輩がすごいって言っても、それは一定以上に伸びていくものじゃない。
　なのにアルクェイドのヤツときたら、まるで際限というものがない。
　初めは先輩に圧されていたくせに、すぐに先輩と互角になって、今では先輩の力を軽く上回ってしまっている―――
lines.label: s270
lines.maoEnglish:
However extraordinary Ciel was, her strength could not continue rising forever.
Arcueid, on the other hand, seemed to possess no limit at all.
Ciel had driven her back at first, only for Arcueid to match her and now surpass her with ease—
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
No matter how amazing Senpai is, her power is not something that goes beyond a certain point.
In contrast, Arcueid seems limitless.
In the beginning, Senpai was overwhelming her, but Arcueid matches her quickly and is now easily surpassing her powers---

lines.japanese:
勝敗はすぐに決した。
　先輩の体が軽く宙にういて、ダン、とゴミのように地面に転がる。
lines.label: s270
lines.maoEnglish:
The battle was decided almost immediately.
Ciel’s body was tossed into the air, then struck the ground and rolled like a piece of refuse.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
The fight is quickly decided.
Senpai's body flies lightly on the air and strikes the ground rolling, like a piece of trash.
lines.mirror_moon:
The fight is quickly decided.

lines.japanese:
「くっ―――」
　うめき声をあげて先輩は立ちあがる。
　でも、それも無駄な抵抗。
　先輩の体は見えない何かに弾かれたように、一層大きく宙に浮いて、地面に倒れこむ。
　先輩は倒れこんだまま動かない。
　じわりと。
公園のレンガ道に広がっていく、赤い血液。
lines.label: s270
lines.maoEnglish:
“Kh—”
Ciel groaned and forced herself upright.
But even that was futile.
As though struck by something invisible, Ciel was hurled still higher and crashed back to earth.
She lay where she had fallen, motionless.
Slowly. Red blood spread across the park’s brick path.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Ka---"
Senpai lets out a cry and stands up.
But that is a useless thing to do.
Senpai's body seems to be shot out by an invisible cannon and flies into the air once more, and hits the ground.
She lies there, not moving.
Blood flows along the park's brick pathway.

lines.japanese:
「先―――輩？」
　返事はない。
　先輩は倒れこんだまま、意識がない。
　そこへ――――容赦なく、それこそ先輩の首でもかき切るような冷酷な目をして、アルクェイドが走りよっていく。
lines.label: s270
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ci—el?”
No answer.
Ciel lay unconscious.
Arcueid rushed toward her without mercy, her eyes cold enough to cut her throat.
lines.mao_english:

lines.japanese:
「――――――あ」

lines.label: s270
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ah…”
My voice would not come.
Arcueid unquestionably meant to “kill” Ciel,
and Ciel no longer had the power to stop her.
“…”
